item.title: SC asks HDFC, ICICI bank to grant prosecution sanction in subvention fraud
item.description: The Supreme Court on Thursday directed HDFC Bank, ICICI Bank, Sammaan Capital and PNB Housing Finance to grant unconditional sanction for prosecution of their officials within a week in alleged subvention scheme frauds involving real estate developers, banks and financial institutions. A bench of Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana warned that the heads of these financial institutions would have to personally appear before it in case of non-compliance. "We direct all the banks or financial institutions referred to above to issue unconditional sanction for prosecution within one week, failing which the CMD and Chairman shall remain present in court to show cause as to why appropriate action be not taken against them," the bench said in its order. Under the subvention scheme, banks disburse the sanctioned amount directly to the accounts of builders, who are then required to pay the EMIs until the flats are handed over to homebuyers. item.title: HC to hear Tata Trusts' plea against Chandra's reappointment on Friday
item.description: The Sir Dorabji Tata Trust (SDTT) and the R.D. Tata Trust (RDTT) on Thursday filed suits in the Bombay High Court against Tata Sons and six of its directors, challenging the reappointment of N Chandrasekaran as executive chairman for a third five-year term. The court will hear the matter on Friday. The SDTT has sought Rs 50 crore, while the RDTT has sought Rs 15 crore in damages, with 18 per cent annual interest. As per the suits, the September 17 Tata Sons board resolution to reappoint Chandrasekaran was invalid because it did not receive the affirmative vote required under Article 121 of the company's Articles of Association (AoA). Senior counsel Janak Dwarkadas, appearing for the two trusts, mentioned the suits on Thursday before a single bench of Justice Arif Doctor, seeking an urgent hearing. item.bs:keywords: Tata Trusts, Tata Sons, N Chandrasekaran, Chandrasekaran reappointment, Bombay High Court, Sir Dorabji Tata Trust, RD Tata Trust, Noel Tata, Venu Srinivasan, Articles of Association, corporate governance, Tata Group

item.title: Sebi appoints auditor to probe Coffee Day Enterprises' fund diversion
item.description: Markets regulator SEBI has appointed a forensic auditor to assist in a probe into the affairs of Coffee Day Enterprises Ltd, following directions from the Securities Appellate Tribunal (SAT). The SAT had on November 5 directed the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) to conduct a fresh, independent and comprehensive investigation into the alleged diversion of Rs 3,535 crore from seven subsidiaries of Coffee Day Enterprises Ltd (CDEL) to Mysore Amalgamated Coffee Estates Ltd (MACEL), an entity linked to the company's promoters. Pursuant to the order dated November 5, 2026 passed by the appellate tribunal, CDEL, in a regulatory filing on Thursday, said "SEBI has, vide its letter dated November 25, 2026, informed the company that CLA Indus Value Consulting has been appointed as the forensic auditor to assist the investigating authority."
